Empirical Framework Meaning: Complaints originate from billing, customer service response latency, local distribution transformer fuses, or localized meter inaccuracies rather than feeder-wide technical drop.
Targeted Utility Directive & Action Plan: Investigate non-PQ causes: Conduct commercial audits, streamline billing customer service dispatching, check local LT line connections.

Empirical Framework Meaning: Severe technical infrastructure degradation causing voltage violations or prolonged outages; directly impacting end-consumers and driving high dissatisfaction.
Targeted Utility Directive & Action Plan: Immediate engineering intervention required: Execute conductor stringing upgrades, balance phase loads, deploy capacitor banks, and overhaul protection switchgear.

Empirical Framework Meaning: Excellent technical performance with minimal consumer grievance logging. Represents the system benchmark standard.
Targeted Utility Directive & Action Plan: Establish as institutional benchmark: Document best-practices, replicate operational topology to adjacent networks.

Empirical Framework Meaning: Hidden structural risks present (poor voltage profiles or low power factor) combined with an abnormally low public reporting rate or passive consumer zone.
Targeted Utility Directive & Action Plan: Execute preventive maintenance: Dispatched maintenance teams for field inspection, implement automated remote terminal unit (RTU) loggers, check for communication gaps.
